topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, course context, and core learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology and carcinogen assessment.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Genetics, "Bad Luck", and Environmental Influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental causes of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic replication errors ("bad luck"), genetic predisposition, and environmental factors supported by geographic epidemiology.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens: Mechanisms of Initiation, Promotion, and Host Vulnerability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific biological, dietary, and chemical carcinogens along with their molecular mechanisms across tumor initiation, inflammatory promotion, and tissue or developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Approaches for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the scientific methodologies used to evaluate and verify carcinogen exposure, including mutational signature profiling, epidemiological biobanking, rodent bioassays, and in vitro Ames testing.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk–Benefit Assessment of Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by synthesizing key takeaways on carcinogen potency and framing environmental exposures within a practical risk-versus-benefit perspective.
